# Imaging

Rasters and computer vision: convolution and the filter family, gradients and edges, corners, blobs and morphology, multiscale pyramids, warps and optical flow. Dependency-free CPU float math built on one value type, `Img`, with the separable-convolution core vectorized to roughly OpenCV's single-threaded speed. Every detector hands back geometry, so results go straight to `lines()`.

## ElectronBrowserTextureSession.kt { #electronbrowsertexturesession-kt }

The Electron process that paints a web page for Field, and the ways a frame of it crosses into
this process.

`ElectronBrowserTextureSession` starts `electron/browser-texture-producer.js` under the Electron
that `./gradlew electronInstall` put in the checkout, passes it the page, the surface size and
the rest as `FIELD_BROWSER_TEXTURE_*` environment variables, and talks to it in JSON lines over a
loopback socket the session opens for the purpose. All of that is platform-neutral; only the GPU
handle transfer is not, and each `BrowserHandleTransport` here is one way to do it: a Mach send
right on macOS, a dma-buf descriptor over `SCM_RIGHTS` on Linux, and an opt-in fallback that
carries the pixels themselves over a second socket for when no handle can cross. The receiver
side of the contract is `ExternalBrowserSurface`, described in
`dev_docs/external_browser_surfaces.md`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/ElectronBrowserTextureSession.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/ElectronBrowserTextureSession/)

## ExternalBrowserSurface.kt { #externalbrowsersurface-kt }

The resident texture that browser paints arrive in: a fixed-size image Field samples like any
other, refreshed from frames a producer offers between draws.

[`ExternalBrowserSurfaceSpec`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt-externalbrowsersurfacespec) fixes size, pixel format and slot count; a producer calls
[`ExternalBrowserSurface.offerFrame`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt--externalbrowsersurface--offerframe) with an [`ExternalBrowserFrame`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt-externalbrowserframe), and the platform import or
copy is recorded in `prepareSampledImagesFor` before the image is bound. [`ExternalBrowserSurfaces.create`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt--externalbrowsersurfaces--create)
picks the macOS, Windows or Linux backend. Frame hand-off is covered by `ExternalBrowserFrameMailboxTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/ExternalBrowserSurface.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/ExternalBrowserSurface/)

### ExternalBrowserImageHandle { #externalbrowsersurface-kt-externalbrowserimagehandle }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">ExternalBrowserImageHandle</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/ExternalBrowserSurface/#L72)

A receiver-side platform handle. IPC is responsible for turning Electron's process-local handle into one of these values. Each value owns the receiver-local handle(s) until a platform importer either consumes them or closes them. Closing a rejected or superseded frame is therefore enough to keep transport resources bounded.

[`handle`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt--externalbrowserframe--handle) is sticky within one `streamId`/`slot`: it may be omitted after the first announcement of that slot, but a new stream must announce its handles again. `releaseToken` is echoed when the GPU has finished copying the frame, allowing Electron's main process to call `OffscreenSharedTexture.release()` safely.

## ExternalBrowserVulkanImports.kt { #externalbrowservulkanimports-kt }

Turning a browser's own GPU allocation into a Vulkan image this process can read: the Windows
D3D11 shared-handle import and the Linux dma-buf import.

Both create a `VkImage` that declares its external handle type, allocate memory dedicated to that
image which imports the handle, and bind the two. The image is only ever a transfer source and a
sampled texture. The Linux side asks the driver whether it can import that format, DRM modifier
and usage before building anything from it, passes each plane's stride and offset as an explicit
layout, and requires the planes to share one allocation, which is what the first Linux backend
supports. macOS does not come through this file: an IOSurface is imported by
`MacExternalBrowserSurface`. What the receivers do with the result, and how far each platform has
got, is in `dev_docs/external_browser_surfaces.md`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/ExternalBrowserVulkanImports.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/ExternalBrowserVulkanImports/)

## FieldUiBrowserTexture.kt { #fielduibrowsertexture-kt }

A live web page as a Field texture: a hidden Electron window renders offscreen and its paints
become an [`ExternalBrowserSurface`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt-externalbrowsersurface) a shader can sample.

[`FieldUiBrowserTexture`](imaging.md#fielduibrowsertexture-kt-fielduibrowsertexture) is the full [`PuppetBrowser`](imaging.md#puppetbrowser-kt-puppetbrowser), so the same object takes navigation, input
and JavaScript. On macOS the frames move GPU-side as IOSurfaces, with no bitmap readback.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/FieldUiBrowserTexture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/FieldUiBrowserTexture/)

## HeadlessPuppetBrowser.kt { #headlesspuppetbrowser-kt }

A Chromium tab with the full browser control plane and no picture, for driving or scraping a page
from a box without a renderer.

[`HeadlessPuppetBrowser`](imaging.md#headlesspuppetbrowser-kt-headlesspuppetbrowser) uses the same Electron producer and protocol as [`FieldUiBrowserTexture`](imaging.md#fielduibrowsertexture-kt-fielduibrowsertexture),
started with frames dropped at the source. `HeadlessPuppetBrowserTest` exercises it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/HeadlessPuppetBrowser.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/HeadlessPuppetBrowser/)

### HeadlessPuppetBrowser { #headlesspuppetbrowser-kt-headlesspuppetbrowser }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">HeadlessPuppetBrowser</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">url</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;about:blank&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1280</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">720</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">deviceScaleFactor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">framesPerSecond</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">projectRoot</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">File</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">locateFieldProjectRoot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PuppetBrowserControl</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/HeadlessPuppetBrowser/#L42)

A Chromium tab with no picture: the whole [`PuppetBrowserControl`](imaging.md#puppetbrowser-kt-puppetbrowsercontrol) plane — navigation, pointer, keyboard, IME, touch, promise-aware JavaScript, the isolated world, arbitrary CDP and the allowlisted page→Field request bridge — with no [`afield.graphics.vulkan.Renderer`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-renderer), no Vulkan surface, no native handle bridge and no readback socket.

## MacExternalBrowserSurface.kt { #macexternalbrowsersurface-kt }

The macOS browser-frame receiver, which imports Electron's IOSurfaces into Vulkan.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/MacExternalBrowserSurface.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/MacExternalBrowserSurface/)

### MacExternalBrowserSurface { #macexternalbrowsersurface-kt-macexternalbrowsersurface }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">MacExternalBrowserSurface</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">spec</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ExternalBrowserSurfaceSpec</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">releaseListener</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">BrowserFrameReleaseListener</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">BrowserFrameReleaseListener</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CopiedExternalBrowserSurface</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">spec</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">releaseListener</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/MacExternalBrowserSurface/#L32)

macOS implementation of [`ExternalBrowserSurface`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt-externalbrowsersurface). A native producer transfers a Mach send right for Electron's process-local IOSurface; this receiver resolves and imports it, while [`CopiedExternalBrowserSurface`](imaging.md#copiedexternalbrowsersurface-kt-copiedexternalbrowsersurface) copies into a stable image and acknowledges only after the fence.

## PuppetBrowser.kt { #puppetbrowser-kt }

The control vocabulary for an offscreen Chromium tab driven from Field: its state, events, and the pointer, key,
touch and JavaScript requests a box sends it.

[`PuppetBrowserControl`](imaging.md#puppetbrowser-kt-puppetbrowsercontrol) is the command plane (navigation, input, JavaScript in the main or isolated world, raw CDP);
[`PuppetBrowser`](imaging.md#puppetbrowser-kt-puppetbrowser) adds an [`ExternalBrowserSurface`](imaging.md#externalbrowsersurface-kt-externalbrowsersurface), so the same tab can be sampled as a texture.
[`HeadlessPuppetBrowser`](imaging.md#headlesspuppetbrowser-kt-headlesspuppetbrowser) implements only the control plane and [`FieldUiBrowserTexture`](imaging.md#fielduibrowsertexture-kt-fielduibrowsertexture) implements both. The wire
encoding is covered by `PuppetBrowserProtocolTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/PuppetBrowser.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/PuppetBrowser/)

### PuppetBrowser { #puppetbrowser-kt-puppetbrowser }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">PuppetBrowser</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PuppetBrowserControl</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">ExternalBrowserSurface</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/PuppetBrowser/#L235)

A [`PuppetBrowserControl`](imaging.md#puppetbrowser-kt-puppetbrowsercontrol) whose pixels are also a stable Field texture — the same Chromium tab, seen from the render loop as well as from the keyboard.

## PuppetBrowserInteraction.kt { #puppetbrowserinteraction-kt }

Input adapters that route mouse, keyboard and controller rays into a [`PuppetBrowser`](imaging.md#puppetbrowser-kt-puppetbrowser).

[`PuppetBrowserUvInput`](imaging.md#puppetbrowserinteraction-kt-puppetbrowseruvinput) turns panel UVs into CSS-pixel pointer events, with click counting;
[`PuppetBrowserWindowInput`](imaging.md#puppetbrowserinteraction-kt-puppetbrowserwindowinput) forwards one Field window's pointer and key stream; [`PuppetBrowserPanel`](imaging.md#puppetbrowserinteraction-kt-puppetbrowserpanel)
places the browser as a world-space rectangle and hit-tests rays against it (orientation is
covered by `PuppetBrowserPanelOrientationTest`).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/PuppetBrowserInteraction.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/PuppetBrowserInteraction/)

## PuppetBrowserPage.kt { #puppetbrowserpage-kt }

Page queries on a puppet browser: an element's text or attribute, a count, a table as rows, and a wait for a condition.

They are thin — each is one `PuppetBrowserControl.evaluate` — and they are here rather than
in a box because the escaping and the null handling are the parts that are easy to get subtly
wrong, and because a shared spelling is what makes two boxes agree about what `text` means.

They run in an isolated world by default. An isolated world sees the same DOM and none of the
page's globals, so a page that has redefined `Array.prototype.map`, shadowed
`document.querySelectorAll` or installed its own `Element.prototype.getAttribute` cannot change
what Field reads out of it; ordinary dashboards ship polyfills that would.

Every one of them works against a `HeadlessPuppetBrowser` with no GPU, and equally against a
`FieldUiBrowserTexture` you are already rendering — the receiver is the control plane, not the
texture.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/PuppetBrowserPage.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/PuppetBrowserPage/)

**Used in:** [Chromium as a native Field surface](../puppet_browser.md)

### WiVRnBrowserInput { #wivrnbrowserinput-kt-wivrnbrowserinput }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">WiVRnBrowserInput</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">browser</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PuppetBrowserControl</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">viewport</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ExternalBrowserSurfaceSpec</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">source</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">WiVRnEventSource</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">layout</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">variant</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">options</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pointerActivity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">otherModifiers</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Set</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">BrowserModifier</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/WiVRnBrowserInput/#L9)

Exclusive, focus-independent Linux input from WiVRn's virtual keyboard and mouse. The mouse lives in browser coordinates, so moving a VR panel never moves its cursor onto another app. Call [`poll`](imaging.md#wivrnbrowserinput-kt--wivrnbrowserinput--poll) once per graphics frame; [`close`](imaging.md#wivrnbrowserinput-kt--wivrnbrowserinput--close) releases keys, buttons and evdev grabs. See `tools/setup_wivrn_input.py` for the narrowly scoped device permissions.

## WindowsExternalBrowserSurface.kt { #windowsexternalbrowsersurface-kt }

Windows import path for Electron browser frames: wraps a D3D11 shared texture, passed as an NT
handle, in a Vulkan image that Field can copy from.

[`WindowsExternalBrowserSurface`](imaging.md#windowsexternalbrowsersurface-kt-windowsexternalbrowsersurface) imports each frame that carries a handle through
`VK_KHR_external_memory_win32`, closes the NT handle after the import, replaces that slot's earlier
image, and retires every slot when the stream id changes. It requires Windows and a device that supports that extension. It has
been compiled but not yet run on Windows.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/browser/WindowsExternalBrowserSurface.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/browser/WindowsExternalBrowserSurface/)

## imaging.kt { #imaging-kt }

CPU image and computer-vision family for the Field stdlib: the raster counterpart to the
time-domain `timeseries.kt` and frequency-domain `spectral.kt` families.

This file, with `imaging_filters.kt`, `imaging_features.kt`, `imaging_geometry.kt` and
`imaging_field.kt`, is the stdlib's image layer: convolution and blurs, gradients, pyramids,
corner and edge features, and warps, over a dependency-free core.

The whole family is built on one value type, [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img):

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val photo  = imgFromFile("cat.png")        // 3-channel sRGB-ish floats in 0..1
val gray   = photo.luma()                  // 1 channel
val edges  = gray.sobelMagnitude()         // 1 channel
val canny  = gray.canny(0.08, 0.20)        // 1 channel binary mask
canny.toFLines()                           // .. straight into Field's drawing layer
```

What the family commits to:

- **Float channels, not bytes.** Every operation is float math in `0..1` (or unbounded, for
  gradients and Laplacians, which legitimately go negative). Nothing quantises mid-pipeline, so
  a 12-stage chain does not accumulate rounding steps. Clamping happens once, on output.
- **Immutable-by-convention value type.** Ops return a new [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img); the backing `FloatArray` is
  public (`data`) so a hot inner loop in a box can write it directly if it wants to.
  Interleaved channel-major-last layout (`data[(y*width + x)*channels + c]`), the same layout
  `BufferedImage`/GL/Vulkan uploads want.
- **1, 3 or 4 channels.** 1 = scalar/gray/mask, 3 = RGB, 4 = RGBA. Nothing else; a 12-channel
  feature tensor is a different problem, and not one this family takes on.
- **No external dependency.** Pure Kotlin plus `javax.imageio` for load/save and
  `afield.media.image.util.PngEncoder` for the AWT-free path used by box output.
- **Live-codeable.** [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img) implements [`ToHTML`](visualization.md#valuevisualizer-kt-tohtml), so evaluating an `Img` in a box (or `img.h`)
  shows the actual picture as an inline thumbnail, not `Img@3f1a2b`.

Out of scope: GPU work (that is Field 4 / StackSL / RectSL), video decoding,
and anything needing a model file.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/image/imaging.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/image/imaging/)

**Used in:** [Imaging and computer vision](../imaging_examples.md), [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md), [Wave Function Collapse examples](../wfc_examples.md)

## imaging_features.kt { #imaging-features-kt }

Edges, corners, lines, blobs and morphology for [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img) — the "find things in the picture" half of
the stdlib imaging family (see `imaging.kt` for the value type and `imaging_filters.kt` for
convolution and gradients).

Everything here reduces pixels to *structure* — a point set, a label map, a list of lines — and
that structure is what `imaging_field.kt` turns into `FLine`s so it lands in Field's drawing
layer rather than staying trapped in a raster.

Every detector here is the textbook algorithm, implemented plainly and documented with the
property a test can check:

| function | what it finds | test invariant |
|---|---|---|
| [`canny`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--canny) | thin, connected edges | a synthetic square yields a 1-pixel-wide closed outline |
| [`harrisCorners`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--harriscorners) / [`shiTomasiCorners`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--shitomasicorners) | corners via the structure tensor | 4 responses at a square's 4 corners |
| [`fastCorners`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--fastcorners) | corners via a brightness circle test | same, and much faster |
| [`houghLines`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--houghlines) | straight lines in polar form | a drawn line is recovered at its `(rho, theta)` |
| [`connectedComponents`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--connectedcomponents) | blobs in a binary mask | N drawn discs give N labels with the right areas |
| [`distanceTransform`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--distancetransform) | distance to the nearest zero | a disc's centre has distance = its radius |

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/image/imaging_features.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/image/imaging_features/)

**Used in:** [Imaging and computer vision](../imaging_examples.md), [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md), [Agent transcript gallery](../agent_transcripts.md)

## imaging_field.kt { #imaging-field-kt }

What makes the imaging family *Field's* rather than a generic CV library: the bridges out of the
raster and into the things Field already draws, colours and displays.

Three bridges:

 1. **Structure → [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline).** Every detector in `imaging_features.kt` produces geometry, and
    geometry in Field is an `FLine`. [`Img.toContourFLines`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--tocontourflines), [`cornersToFLines`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--cornerstoflines), [`linesToFLines`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--linestoflines),
    [`FlowField.toFLines`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--toflines) and [`Img.isoContourFLines`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--isocontourflines) hand you drawable lines, so a Canny result
    goes straight into the same drawing/animation/export machinery as anything hand-drawn.
 2. **Scalar → colour.** [`Img.colormap`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--colormap) runs a 1-channel response image through the same
    [`Colormaps`](graphics.md#colormaps-kt-colormaps) tables RectSL's `heat`/`bars`/`scatter` use, so a Harris response, a distance
    transform and a RectSL chart are coloured by one source of truth.
 3. **Value → screen.** [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img) is a [`afield.ui.visualization.ToHTML`](visualization.md#valuevisualizer-kt-tohtml), so evaluating one in a box shows the picture;
    [`Box.showImg`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--showimg) pushes a full-size version to an output channel, and [`Box.showImgGrid`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--showimggrid) lays
    several out side by side with captions — the fastest way to see a whole pipeline at once.

The scalar-field bridge runs the other way too: [`Img.asScalarField2D`](imaging.md#imaging-field-kt--asscalarfield2d) adapts an [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img) to the
`ScalarField2D` type `contours.kt` marches, so Field's existing marching-squares iso-contour
extractor works on image data with no glue.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/image/imaging_field.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/image/imaging_field/)

**Used in:** [Imaging and computer vision](../imaging_examples.md), [Wave Function Collapse examples](../wfc_examples.md), [Spatial artificial life](../alife_examples.md)

## imaging_filters.kt { #imaging-filters-kt }

Convolution, smoothing, gradients and multiscale pyramids for [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img) — the filter half of the
stdlib imaging family (see `imaging.kt` for the value type, `imaging_features.kt` for edges,
corners and blobs).

Everything here is per-channel: a 3-channel image blurs each of R, G, B independently. Filters
that only make sense on a scalar field ([`sobel`](imaging.md#imaging-filters-kt--sobel), [`laplacian`](imaging.md#imaging-filters-kt--laplacian), …) take the [`Img.luma`](imaging.md#imaging-kt--luma) of a colour
input automatically rather than erroring, because that is what you meant.

Two performance-relevant choices:

- **Separable when possible.** Gaussian and box blurs run as two 1-D passes (`O(k)` per pixel,
  not `O(k²)`). [`convolveSeparable`](imaging.md#imaging-filters-kt--convolveseparable) is public so your own separable kernels get the same
  treatment, and [`convolve2D`](imaging.md#imaging-filters-kt--convolve2d) exists both as a general fallback and as the naive reference the
  unit tests check the separable path against.
- **Box blur is a running sum.** [`boxBlur`](imaging.md#imaging-filters-kt--boxblur) is `O(1)` per pixel regardless of radius, so a
  radius-40 mean is as cheap as radius-1. Three box passes approximate a Gaussian closely
  (see [`boxBlurApproxGaussian`](imaging.md#imaging-filters-kt--boxblurapproxgaussian)) if you need a very large sigma cheaply.

## imaging_geometry.kt { #imaging-geometry-kt }

Geometry and motion for [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img): affine and perspective warps, homography estimation from point
correspondences (DLT + RANSAC), and pyramidal Lucas–Kanade optical flow.

This is the part of the imaging family that relates *two* pictures rather than transforming one.
The through-line is:

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val pts   = a.goodFeaturesToTrack(120)                 // where is there anything to track?
val flow  = opticalFlowLK(a, b, pts)                   // where did each of those go?
val fit   = findHomographyRansac(flow.sourcePoints(), flow.targetPoints())
val warped = b.warpPerspective(fit.homography.inverse()) // undo the motion
```

The linear algebra is self-contained (a 9x9 Jacobi eigen-solver and a 6x6 Gaussian
elimination), because a 3x3 homography does not justify a dependency and the whole point of this
family is that it works headless in a box with nothing installed.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/image/imaging_geometry.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/image/imaging_geometry/)

**Used in:** [Imaging and computer vision](../imaging_examples.md), [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md)

## imaging_overlay.kt { #imaging-overlay-kt }

Drawing [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline)s into an [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img), in software and without AWT.

[`Img.drawFLines`](imaging.md#imaging-overlay-kt--drawflines) is the whole surface. It resamples the image up by a scale factor and blends
each line over it, reading `color`, `thickness`, `pointed`, `filled` and the rest from the line's
own properties the way Field draws it on the canvas; round-capped segments and even-odd fills are
rasterised here, each with a pixel of antialiasing. What comes back is another [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img), so an
overlay costs no GPU, no window and no AWT font or toolkit, and `showImgGrid` can show it
wherever a box runs.

## imaging_simd.kt { #imaging-simd-kt }

The SIMD span kernels the imaging filters are built out of.

### Why this file exists

The scalar filter layer reads every sample through [`Img.get`](imaging.md#imaging-kt--img--get), which per multiply-add costs a
range check, a channel clamp and a `when` over [`Border`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-border). That is correct and readable, and it is
also unvectorizable: C2 cannot hoist a branch whose outcome depends on the loop index out of the
inner loop, so a 3-tap Sobel pays three bounds-checked calls per sample.

The fix is not to make the accessor faster — it is to stop calling it in the interior. Because
[`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img) stores samples interleaved (`data[(y * width + x) * channels + c]`), *both* passes of a
separable convolution address contiguous memory:

- **Vertical.** For a fixed output row, tap `t` reads the whole of source row `y + t - r`. The
  border decision is therefore *per row*, not per pixel: resolve the row index once and the
  entire row is a straight span. Every row takes the fast path.
- **Horizontal.** Adding `(t - r) * channels` to a flat index moves to the same channel of the
  pixel `t - r` columns over. So for a fixed tap the whole interior of a row is, again, a
  straight span — only the `r` columns at each end need the general accessor.

### The one primitive that matters: `stencil`

Both observations reduce a convolution — separable *or* dense — to the same shape: a destination
span is a weighted sum of `k` source spans at fixed element offsets. That is `stencil`, and it
keeps the running sum **in a vector register** across all taps, so `k` taps cost `k` reads and
**one** write.

The alternative — accumulate in memory, one `axpy` per tap — costs `k` reads *and* `k`
read-modify-writes. For the sigma-2 Gaussian used in the benchmark (`radius 8`, 17 taps) that is
17 write passes over the image where one would do, and it is why `stencil` rather than `axpy` is
the inner loop of everything here. `axpy` survives only for the handful of border rows where each
tap resolves to a *different*, border-dependent source row and there is no single offset to fold.

### Why the main loop keeps four accumulators

`stencil` is a chain of `k` dependent FMAs into one accumulator. On Apple silicon an FMA has ~4
cycles of latency and can issue ~4 per cycle, so a single-accumulator 17-tap chain runs at
latency, not throughput — about 16x off peak. The main loop therefore keeps **four** independent
accumulators (four output chunks in flight), which converts the chain into something the machine
can pipeline, then falls back to one chunk at a time and finally to scalar for the tail. This is
the difference between "uses the Vector API" and "is fast".

### Decimation, without a gather

A pass that throws half its output away should not compute it. Halving *rows* is free (just skip
them), but halving *columns* makes the reads stride-2, which on NEON means a gather. `splitByPhase`
avoids it: output `x` reads source pixel `2x + s`, whose parity is fixed by the parity of `s`. So
even-offset taps only ever read even-indexed pixels and odd-offset taps only odd ones. Split the
row into its even and odd pixels once — into one scratch buffer, laid out even-half then odd-half,
so a single `stencil` call can address both — and every tap is unit-stride again. This is the
polyphase decomposition, and it is what makes [`Img.pyrDown`](imaging.md#imaging-filters-kt--pyrdown) a half-resolution filter rather than a
full-resolution one with a discard at the end.

### On FMA

These kernels use fused multiply-add: one rounding per tap instead of two. Results therefore
differ from the scalar reference in the last ulp — more accurate, not less, but not bit-identical.
`ImagingSimdTest` asserts agreement to `2e-6f`, which is four orders of magnitude above this.

## NodeTool.kt { #nodetool-kt }

Locates a `node` binary new enough to run the JavaScript this repository generates, for the tests
and tools that shell out to Node.

Generated Kotlin/JS uses `globalThis` (Node 12+) and optional chaining (Node 14+). A shell that
inherits several `nvm` bin directories can put an old Node first on `PATH`, and taking the first
match then fails inside a temporary `.js` file with a `SyntaxError` that says nothing about the
binary. [`NodeTool.resolveNode`](imaging.md#nodetool-kt--nodetool--resolvenode) therefore scans `PATH` for a candidate that meets the version floor
rather than the first one that exists.

Resolution order, first match wins:

1. `AFIELD_NODE` / `NODE`, if set and executable. An explicit override is honoured even below the
   floor, so asking for a binary by path gets that binary, and a clear failure if it is too old.
2. Every `PATH` entry, in order, whose `node` reports a major version at or above the floor
   ([`NodeTool.DEFAULT_MIN_MAJOR`](imaging.md#nodetool-kt--nodetool--default-min-major) unless the caller passes one).
3. The repository-local Node that Gradle installs under `.gradle/nodejs`, so JS-backed tests work
   under a minimal `PATH`.

Nothing qualifying gives `null`. Call sites decide whether that is a skip or a failure, and
[`NodeTool.unavailableMessage`](imaging.md#nodetool-kt--nodetool--unavailablemessage) renders the reason either way.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/image/util/NodeTool.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/image/util/NodeTool/)

## PngEncoder.kt { #pngencoder-kt }

Encodes ARGB pixels, or an RGBA `ByteBuffer` read back from the GPU, into PNG bytes without AWT or
`javax.imageio`.

Output is 8-bit RGBA (PNG colour type 6), one unfiltered scanline per row, compressed with
`java.util.zip.Deflater`, with an `sRGB` chunk. [`PngEncoder.encode`](imaging.md#pngencoder-kt--pngencoder--encode) takes one ARGB `Int` per pixel;
[`PngEncoder.encodeFromBuffer`](imaging.md#pngencoder-kt--pngencoder--encodefrombuffer) takes a readback buffer and can flip it vertically and force alpha
to opaque.

## DlssReconstruction.kt { #dlssreconstruction-kt }

DLSS super resolution, DLAA and Ray Reconstruction through NVIDIA NGX, as a pass recorded into a Vulkan command buffer.

[`DlssReconstruction`](imaging.md#dlssreconstruction-kt-dlssreconstruction) takes render-resolution color, depth and motion ([`ReconstructionInputs`](imaging.md#dlssreconstruction-kt-reconstructioninputs)), plus
[`RayReconstructionGuides`](imaging.md#dlssreconstruction-kt-rayreconstructionguides) when ray reconstruction is on, and writes an output-resolution texture.
Each frame is described by a [`ReconstructionFrame`](imaging.md#dlssreconstruction-kt-reconstructionframe): its index, the [`ReconstructionJitter`](imaging.md#dlssreconstruction-kt-reconstructionjitter) the scene
was sampled with (`ReconstructionJitter.halton` gives a sequence sized to the upscale ratio),
frame time and pre-exposure. Call `reset` on camera cuts and live edits so history is discarded.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/reconstruction/DlssReconstruction.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/reconstruction/DlssReconstruction/)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DlssReconstruction</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">inputSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ReconstructionSize</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">outputSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ReconstructionSize</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">mode</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ReconstructionMode</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rayReconstruction</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/reconstruction/DlssReconstruction/#L73)

One mono view. Construct/edit/evaluate/close on the render thread, outside a render pass. Query `recommend` before allocating the scene targets. Recreate on resolution/mode/format change; the old instance retires behind Field's GPU completion queue. Failure leaves caller's source intact. SR is independent of ray tracing. UI and unsupported animated layers belong after this pass.

## NgxSupport.kt { #ngxsupport-kt }

Detection of NVIDIA NGX support and the sizes and modes DLSS reconstruction accepts.

[`NgxSupport`](imaging.md#ngxsupport-kt-ngxsupport) reports whether DLAA, DLSS super resolution and Ray Reconstruction are available on
a device; ordinary rendering never requires NGX. [`ReconstructionMode`](imaging.md#ngxsupport-kt-reconstructionmode) lists the quality modes,
and [`ReconstructionRecommendation`](imaging.md#ngxsupport-kt-reconstructionrecommendation) holds the optimal, minimum and maximum input sizes for an output.

## PathTracedReconstruction.kt { #pathtracedreconstruction-kt }

Runs a path tracer, converts its output into ray reconstruction guides, and denoises it with DLSS Ray Reconstruction, in one ordered pass.

[`PathTracedReconstruction`](imaging.md#pathtracedreconstruction-kt-pathtracedreconstruction) takes an uninstalled `PathTracingRenderer`, owns its dispatch and
closes it. `view` selects the raw, progressive or reconstructed image, and `gpuMilliseconds`
reports the GPU time of tracing, guide conversion and NGX together.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/reconstruction/PathTracedReconstruction.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/reconstruction/PathTracedReconstruction/)

### PathTracedReconstruction { #pathtracedreconstruction-kt-pathtracedreconstruction }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PathTracedReconstruction</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">tracer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PathTracingRenderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">outputSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ReconstructionSize</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="nc">ReconstructionSize</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">tracer</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">width</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">tracer</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">height</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">mode</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ReconstructionMode</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="nc">ReconstructionMode</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">DLAA</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s">&quot;path-reconstruction&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Target</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/reconstruction/PathTracedReconstruction/#L28)

One ordered path-trace -> raw guides -> NGX pass. This owner records the tracer exactly once, and closes it; [`install`](imaging.md#pathtracedreconstruction-kt--pathtracedreconstruction--install) takes a tracer from pathTracingHere(...) off its standalone passes. The raw and progressive sources remain inspectable at all times. Camera motion reprojects; call [`reset`](imaging.md#pathtracedreconstruction-kt--pathtracedreconstruction--reset) on cuts and appearance changes. Tracer property and shader revisions reset RR automatically. Recreate this owner to change input/output sizes.

## RayReconstructionDemo.kt { #rayreconstructiondemo-kt }

A direct-lighting scene lit by RTXDI whose output can be switched between raw, spatially denoised and DLSS Ray Reconstruction paths.

[`RayReconstructionDemo`](imaging.md#rayreconstructiondemo-kt-rayreconstructiondemo) reuses `DirectLightingDemo` for the G-buffer and lighting, builds the
guide images ray reconstruction needs, and runs two [`DlssReconstruction`](imaging.md#dlssreconstruction-kt-dlssreconstruction) instances at native
resolution. Setting `path` resets history and changes which image is shown.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/reconstruction/RayReconstructionDemo.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/reconstruction/RayReconstructionDemo/)

## ReconstructionDemo.kt { #reconstructiondemo-kt }

A small editable raster scene for trying DLAA and DLSS super resolution without ray tracing.

[`ReconstructionDemo`](imaging.md#reconstructiondemo-kt-reconstructiondemo) renders color, depth and motion at the input resolution recommended for its
[`ReconstructionMode`](imaging.md#ngxsupport-kt-reconstructionmode) and hands the three to [`DlssReconstruction`](imaging.md#dlssreconstruction-kt-dlssreconstruction). Leave `mode` null to see the
unjittered source at output resolution. `reload` swaps in new vertex and fragment shaders, and
`reset` discards reconstruction history after a scene edit.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/reconstruction/ReconstructionDemo.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/reconstruction/ReconstructionDemo/)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">ReconstructionMotionGpuSmoke</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/reconstruction/ReconstructionMotionGpuSmoke/#L26)

Compare real NGX history fed pixel motion with the same motion encoded as Field UV velocity. An untagged UV control must disagree, so equality cannot pass by ignoring motion on both paths. ## ElectronRTTView.kt { #electronrttview-kt }

Shows a Field 4 render target live in a box's output area in the Field Electron app, sharing GPU
surfaces with Electron instead of reading pixels back.

[`ElectronRTTView`](imaging.md#electronrttview-kt-electronrttview) is the entry point: render into its [`ElectronRTTView.rtt`](imaging.md#electronrttview-kt--electronrttview--rtt) and `display` its
[`ElectronRTTView.html`](imaging.md#electronrttview-kt--electronrttview--html). Works on macOS and on Linux under native Wayland; outside Electron the
widget says it needs the app.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/stream/ElectronRTTView.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/stream/ElectronRTTView/)

## FieldEncodeProcess.kt { #fieldencodeprocess-kt }

The JVM side of the `field-encode` helper, which encodes Field render targets (VideoToolbox on
macOS, the `field-encode-linux` build on Linux) and streams them to the visionOS app.

[`FieldEncodeProcess`](imaging.md#fieldencodeprocess-kt-fieldencodeprocess) starts the helper and exchanges newline-delimited JSON with it; image data
never passes through this pipe. [`FieldRTTStreamer`](imaging.md#fieldrttstreamer-kt-fieldrttstreamer) is the usual way to drive it from a box.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/stream/FieldEncodeProcess.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/stream/FieldEncodeProcess/)

On Linux, pass `fdSurfaces` + `fdSocket` — the helper has no `alloc` (it can't allocate a Vulkan image itself), and a raw fd number can't travel over JSON (it's per-process, not a system-wide handle like an IOSurfaceID): the real fds cross over an SCM_RIGHTS handoff on `fdSocket` instead (see [`afield.graphics.texture.UnixFdPass`](graphics.md#unixfdpass-kt-unixfdpass) — caller sends them right after this command), and only `size`/`rowPitch` travel on the wire, in the same order as the fds sent over the socket. |

## FieldRTTStreamer.kt { #fieldrttstreamer-kt }

Streams a Field 4 render target to the visionOS app as video (HEVC by default), through the `field-encode` helper.

[`FieldRTTStreamer`](imaging.md#fieldrttstreamer-kt-fieldrttstreamer) owns a ring of shared surfaces that a box renders into; each frame is handed to the encoder once
the GPU has finished it. Works on macOS (VideoToolbox) and Linux (NVENC).

## LinuxElectronImportProbe.kt { #linuxelectronimportprobe-kt }

A standalone Linux probe that hands Electron one finished Vulkan image and reads back its verdict
on the pixels.

It clears a 64×64 dma-buf-exportable [`RenderToTexture`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture) to a known colour, copies that back through
a staging buffer to confirm the Field side is not blank, releases the image to
`VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_EXTERNAL` behind a waited fence, and sends the descriptor over [`UnixFdPass`](graphics.md#unixfdpass-kt-unixfdpass) with
the plane's stride and offset and the allocation's DRM modifier written beside it as
`texture.json`. Then it waits up to a minute for the Node side's `result.json`. Start
`tools/electron_dmabuf_probe/main.js` first; the single argument is the directory the two sides
exchange evidence in, and `native/field-fdpass` has to be built.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/stream/LinuxElectronImportProbe.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/stream/LinuxElectronImportProbe/)

## OpticalFlowDemo.kt { #opticalflowdemo-kt }

A self-contained optical-flow demonstration that renders two warped test images, measures the motion between them,
and drives a feedback image with it.

[`OpticalFlowDemo`](imaging.md#opticalflowdemo-kt-opticalflowdemo) builds its own inputs, so it runs without a camera or video source; it is a starting point for
wiring [`opticalFlow`](imaging.md#opticalflowoperation-kt--opticalflow) output into shaders.

## OpticalFlowOperation.kt { #opticalflowoperation-kt }

The shared contract for dense optical flow in Field: the [`OpticalFlowOperation`](imaging.md#opticalflowoperation-kt-opticalflowoperation) interface, the
[`OpticalFlowBackend`](imaging.md#opticalflowoperation-kt-opticalflowbackend) choice, and the [`opticalFlow`](imaging.md#opticalflowoperation-kt--opticalflow) factory that picks a backend for a renderer.

Both backends, [`HardwareOpticalFlow`](imaging.md#hardwareopticalflow-kt-hardwareopticalflow) and [`PyramidOpticalFlow`](imaging.md#pyramidopticalflow-kt-pyramidopticalflow), take two images of one renderer and
write the same RGBA32F flow texture, so code that samples [`OpticalFlowOperation.output`](imaging.md#opticalflowoperation-kt--opticalflowoperation--output) does not
depend on which one ran.

## PyramidOpticalFlow.kt { #pyramidopticalflow-kt }

The portable optical-flow backend: coarse-to-fine Lucas–Kanade built from ordinary fragment passes,
for devices without a hardware motion engine.

[`PyramidOpticalFlow`](imaging.md#pyramidopticalflow-kt-pyramidopticalflow) is what `OpticalFlowBackend.AUTO` picks on any device without
VK_NV_optical_flow enabled, MoltenVK included.

## WebRTC.kt { #webrtc-kt }

WebRTC video for Field 4 graphics: publish a render target to a classroom, and sample anyone's
published stream as a texture.

[`webrtcSink`](imaging.md#webrtc-kt--webrtcsink) publishes what you render into its `rtt`; [`webrtcSource`](imaging.md#webrtc-kt--webrtcsource) is a texture showing one
publisher; [`webrtcPublishers`](imaging.md#webrtc-kt--webrtcpublishers) is the live list of who is publishing. They join aaaframe's
ShaderTrinket network (set `WebRTCNetwork.default`, or `AFIELD_WEBRTC_SERVER`), where browser
ShaderTrinkets see a Field sink as one more publisher, or Field's own relay for a LAN of Field
instances. Chromium does the WebRTC; Field moves the frames on the GPU and relays signalling.
How and why: `dev_docs/WEBRTC_SOURCES_SINKS.md`.

## WebRTCPublish.kt { #webrtcpublish-kt }

Publishing what Field renders as a WebRTC stream, and the colour conversion that makes the stream
look like the window.

[`webrtcPublish`](imaging.md#webrtcpublish-kt--webrtcpublish) is the one call a box makes: it creates a sink of the size you ask for and adds a
copy pass that samples your source into it every frame. The copy is a full-screen triangle whose
fragment shader is written for the source and target formats it finds, so an 8-bit UNORM source
holding display values and a float or `_SRGB` one holding linear light both come out looking the
same. `WebRTCPublishTest` pins which of the four pairings converts and which passes the colour
through, and compiles every variant. The sink itself, the sources and the networks are in
`WebRTC.kt`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/webrtc/WebRTCPublish.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/webrtc/WebRTCPublish/)

## WebRTCRoutes.kt { #webrtcroutes-kt }

The signalling a Field WebRTC sink or source gets from its own server: the
`/ws/webrtc-signaling?network=<id>` WebSocket its page exchanges signalling over, and
`/api/webrtc-config?network=<id>`, which answers with that network's login and ICE servers.

Installed beside Field's other WebSockets. Both answer only for networks box code has registered
(`WebRTCNetwork.aaaframe`/`join`, or the local relay), so a client cannot make Field connect
anywhere else; the guard decisions are in `dev_docs/server_surface_inventory.md`. A local network
is relayed inside this process and every other one is forwarded upstream to aaaframe;
`WebRTCSignalingTest` drives the socket both ways.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/webrtc/WebRTCRoutes.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/webrtc/WebRTCRoutes/)

## WebRTCSignaling.kt { #webrtcsignaling-kt }

WebRTC signalling for Field's sources and sinks: the networks a page can join, the relay on
Field's own server, and the bridge to an aaaframe classroom.

Pages never connect to a signalling server themselves. They open
`/ws/webrtc-signaling?network=<id>` on Field, and Field either relays the messages itself
(`WebRTCNetwork.local`) or copies them to and from aaaframe's `/ws/shadertrinket-signaling`
(`WebRTCNetwork.aaaframe`), adding the student's session cookie. The messages are aaaframe's in
both cases, so the page code is the same. The design is in `dev_docs/WEBRTC_SOURCES_SINKS.md`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/webrtc/WebRTCSignaling.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/webrtc/WebRTCSignaling/)
